$comment: Options for the mqtt connector. Keys map 1:1 to MQTTConnector.__init__ kwargs (spread by main.create_classes) — keep in lockstep with the constructor; tests/test_config.py enforces this. Scalars also accept "string" and "null": interpolation runs AFTER validation, so a "${MQTT_PORT}" arrives at the constructor as a str. It coerces each one through api/options.py.

port.$comment: 1883 plain, 8883 TLS. Coerced, because paho compares it against an int inside connect() — an unresolved ${VAR} used to be a TypeError on the supervised worker thread rather than a config warning.

version.$comment: Accepts null so an unresolved "${MQTT_VERSION}" warns and falls back to 3.1.1. MQTTVersion is a StrEnum, so it would otherwise raise ValueError — which create_classes does not catch, taking the whole process down.

tls.$comment: Coerced, and this one used to fail silently rather than loudly: tls is only read for truthiness, and the string "false" is truthy — so an operator disabling TLS through an environment variable got TLS anyway.
